market_summary: Monday's US session (Columbus Day, bond market shut) ended mixed: S&P 500 -0.06% to 7,807, Nasdaq -0.44% to 27,246, Dow +0.38% to 51,851, while the Philadelphia chip index fell 2.7% to a three-week low as Micron, SanDisk and Western Digital sold off on China's CXMT DRAM progress. Brent settled +1.8% at $106.65 and WTI +2.1% at $93.74 as the Saudi airport attacks outweighed Trump's Russia-Ukraine 'energy ceasefire', which Zelenskiy said Russia looks unlikely to accept; December gold fell 0.6% to $4,191, the dollar index hit an 18-month high of 102.59, and Cleveland Fed's Hammack said policy should move 'relatively quickly' toward restrictive. Tuesday in Asia the memory sell-off deepened: KOSPI -5.47% to 6,035 after a sell-side sidecar (SK hynix -10.1%, Samsung -7.4%), Taiex -1.95% to 48,341, Nikkei about -1.8% near 67,800 on its return from the holiday (Kioxia, SoftBank, Tokyo Electron led), Shanghai about -1% and Shenzhen -2.2%, Hang Seng -0.4% and Hang Seng Tech -1.5% at the midday break, and the ASX 200 flat (+0.008%) as banks offset tech -4.4%. RBA minutes showed the 4.60% hike was unanimous and the Board is ready to go again if needed. US futures at 01:33 ET: Nasdaq 100 -0.5%, S&P 500 -0.1%, Dow +0.3%; Brent -1.1% to $105.52, WTI -1.2% to $92.63; bitcoin dipped below $82,000 on Oct 12 before recovering above $83,000. Next: JPM, Wells, Citi, Goldman 22:00-22:30 AEDT Tue; Apple home event 00:00 AEDT Wed; US open 00:30 AEDT Wed; China CPI/PPI 12:30 AEDT Wed with September trade data also Wed; ASML 16:00 AEDT Wed; US CPI 23:30 AEDT Wed (core seen +0.2%), BAC and MS before that open; Anthropic investor session Thu AEDT; AU jobs 11:30 AEDT Thu; TSMC 17:00 AEDT Thu; PPI, retail sales and claims 23:30 AEDT Thu; Warsh 14:30 AEDT Fri; FOMC blackout from Sat Oct 17; China Q3 GDP 13:00 AEDT Mon Oct 19; Netflix 07:01 AEDT Wed Oct 21; Meta (now confirmed) 07:30 AEDT Thu Oct 22.

AMZN.reason: Fell 1.1% Monday after the WSJ reported Amazon is in talks to buy AI chip-software startup Decart for about $7 billion; Decart was valued near $4 billion in May and no deal is signed. A small deal for Amazon's size that supports Trainium. Alexa tablets go on sale Wed Oct 14; Q3 about Fri Oct 30 07:00 AEDT. Hold.

AXOS.reason: No company news. JPMorgan, Wells Fargo, Citi and Goldman report tonight before the US open (22:00-22:30 AEDT Tue), the first read on deposit costs and credit ahead of Axos's fiscal Q1 call Fri Oct 30 08:00 AEDT. US CPI Wed 23:30 AEDT. Hold.

BABA.reason: US ADR slipped 0.5% Monday, giving back little of Friday's 5.4% jump; Hong Kong shares opened 0.5% lower Tuesday as Hang Seng Tech fell about 1% on chip weakness. No company news. China CPI, PPI and trade data Wed 12:30 AEDT; results Nov 24. Hold.

ENPH.reason: Fell 4.0% Monday with no company or solar-policy news found; the dollar index hit an 18-month high and oil rose 2%, while rates stay high (Mortgage News Daily's 30-year was last 7.48%). US CPI Wed 23:30 AEDT is the week's rate test; Q3 call Wed Oct 28 07:30 AEDT. Watch.

FIGR.reason: Down 0.3% Monday on no company news, holding most of Friday's 3.4% gain; the Q3 results date is still unannounced. Bank results tonight (22:00-22:30 AEDT) and US CPI Wed 23:30 AEDT drive the rate-sensitive names this week. Hold.

GOOGL.reason: Up 0.3% Monday while the Nasdaq fell 0.4% and chips sold off, the steadiest of the AI holdings. No company news; the communications sector led the S&P with +1%. Q3 results late October. Add stays.

LDI.reason: Bounced 3.6% Monday on no news after Friday's 9% drop to a 52-week low. The bond market was shut for Columbus Day, so Mortgage News Daily's 30-year is still the Friday reading of 7.48%. Still below the NYSE one-dollar threshold with the cure period to February; CPI Wed 23:30 AEDT is the next rate test. Trim.

META.reason: Rose 3.4% Monday after Zuckerberg said Meta has caught up with rivals on frontier AI models and hinted at a strong upcoming model, the best move among the holdings. Still no New Mexico penalty ruling: the state wants $35-40 billion, Meta asks for no more than $1.53 billion, and the judge plans to rule by late October. Meta confirmed Q3 results for Wed Oct 21 after the US close (call 07:30 AEDT Thu Oct 22), a week earlier than expected. Hold.

MRVL.reason: Fell 3.4% Monday as the Philadelphia chip index dropped 2.7%, its fourth straight loss, and optical names Lumentum, Ciena and Coherent fell 8-10%. No company news. Taiwan fell 1.95% Tuesday; TSMC's Q3 call Thu 17:00 AEDT is the week's first read on AI demand. Hold.

MU.reason: Fell 3.9% Monday as China's CXMT denser-DRAM plan hit memory names (SanDisk -6%), then Korea deepened the slide Tuesday: KOSPI closed down 5.5% with SK hynix -10.1% and Samsung -7.4%, so expect more pressure tonight. CXMT's server parts are an end-2026 target and TrendForce calls the date ambitious, while DDR5 spot set another high Tuesday. Hold, but three sessions down.

NFLX.reason: Up 0.4% Monday. The 5% job cuts Puck reported Friday (about 800-850 roles) are still not confirmed by Netflix. Q3 results Wed Oct 21 07:00 AEDT, guided to $12.86 billion revenue (+12%) and a 33.2% operating margin. Hold into the print.

NVDA.reason: Fell 1.3% Monday, far less than the chip index's 2.7% drop. Nothing new on the FT-reported Reflection AI talks (acquisition, acqui-hire or bigger stake; Reflection's last valuation was $25 billion pre-money). TSMC's Q3 call Thu 17:00 AEDT is the first supply-chain read, then GTC Berlin Oct 20-22. Hold.

RKT.reason: Fell 5.3% Monday with no company news found, a third straight decline. The bond market was shut, so Mortgage News Daily's 30-year is still Friday's 7.48% and Freddie Mac's weekly 7.40% is the highest since 2023. Bank results tonight 22:00-22:30 AEDT and CPI Wed 23:30 AEDT; Q3 around Oct 29. Watch.

TSM.reason: ADR fell 2.0% Monday with the chip selloff, then Taipei shares fell 2.0% Tuesday as the Taiex lost 1.95% on Korea's memory rout. TSMC's own numbers are unaffected: Q3 revenue already reported at about $46.7 billion against a $45.4 billion consensus. Results Thu Oct 15 17:00 AEDT. Add stays.

STRIPE.reason: No new round, tender or secondary mark reported; the last company tender was February at $159 billion, so the mark multiple stays 2.27. No company news since the Oct 6 FedEx Dataworks partnership. Hold.

OPENAI.reason: The $30 billion round at about a $1.4 trillion pre-money valuation is still in talks with an MGX-led UAE group (up to $10 billion) and BlackRock, with no close reported, so the mark multiple stays 5.43. No new deals or follow-up on the safety-researcher firings found. Anthropic's investor session Thu AEDT is the week's private-AI reference. Hold.

headlines: Memory rout spread: KOSPI fell 5.5% Tuesday, SK hynix 10%, Samsung 7%, after Micron lost 3.9% Monday on China's CXMT DRAM plan.
Chip index fell 2.7% Monday, a fourth straight loss; Marvell -3.4%, TSMC -2% in New York and again in Taipei.
Meta rose 3.4% after Zuckerberg said it caught up on frontier AI; Q3 results now Oct 21, 07:30 AEDT Thu Oct 22.
WSJ: Amazon in talks to buy AI startup Decart for about $7B; Amazon fell 1.1%, Alphabet edged up 0.3%.
Physical demand held: DDR5 spot set another high Tuesday and H100 rent rose 2c to $2.85.
Next: banks 22:00 AEDT tonight, Apple 00:00 AEDT Wed, ASML 16:00 AEDT Wed, US CPI 23:30 AEDT Wed, TSMC 17:00 AEDT Thu.
